content: Ruby HTTP client for Rails 8 service objects calling a third-party API: community consensus and download volume both favour Faraday (2.14.3, 1.24 billion downloads, runtime deps faraday-net_http/json/logger only). Faraday earns its place over stdlib Net::HTTP mainly for (a) connection-level defaults - base_url, static headers, JSON request/response middleware, open/read/write timeouts - and (b) the built-in Faraday::Adapter::Test stub adapter, which gives deterministic unit tests without adding WebMock. faraday-retry is a SEPARATE gem in Faraday 2.x (2.4.0); its interval/backoff sleeps inside the calling thread, so it is the wrong layer for a background-job integration where ActiveJob retry_on already provides durable non-blocking backoff. Net::HTTP with a thin wrapper remains a legitimate zero-gem option for a small (~6 endpoint) surface but costs ~80 lines of hand-rolled timeout/JSON/error-mapping plus a test-stubbing gem.
